title: Trump: Steve Bannon tells followers to ‘take action' to stop the stolen election
description_short: Trump: Steve Bannon tells followers to ‘take action' to stop the stolen election
description_medium: On January 5, 2021, Steve Bannon posted “TAKE ACTION. THEY ARE TRYING TO STEAL THE ELECTION” in a Facebook group. The Capitol was attacked the following day. The linked account says Bannon had spoken with Donald Trump multiple times about efforts to overturn the result and had used Facebook pages and groups to spread election claims. Facebook had removed seven of his pages in November, but the group remained active.
description_long: The post appeared the day before the January 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, as Congress was preparing to count the electoral votes. In a Facebook group, Bannon wrote, “TAKE ACTION. THEY ARE TRYING TO STEAL THE ELECTION.” The linked timeline says the group had been created two days after the election under the name “Stop the Steal,” then renamed after Facebook shut down another group with that title. It says the group promoted baseless claims that the election was stolen and QAnon conspiracies. Facebook had removed seven pages operated by Bannon in November for spreading election disinformation, but the timeline reports that the ban did not extend to this group. The entry also says Trump and Bannon spoke repeatedly around this period about reversing the election result. The timing and wording of the post are documented here as part of the mobilization environment before January 6. The sequence alone does not prove that Bannon directed the attack or that the post caused it. It does show a prominent Trump ally urging followers to act on a false election narrative less than a day before the Capitol was stormed.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Steve Bannon tells followers to ‘take action' to stop the stolen election
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Steve Bannon tells followers to ‘take action' to stop the stolen election

notes: Expanded from the supplied synopsis and linked timeline; does not claim the post caused or directed the Capitol attack.

title: Donald Trump sells entire 45th floor of Trump World Tower to Saudi Arabia
description_short: Donald Trump sells entire 45th floor of Trump World Tower to Saudi Arabia
description_medium: In June 2001, Donald Trump sold five apartments occupying the 45th floor of Trump World Tower to Saudi Arabia for $4.5 million, according to documents reported by the New York Daily News. The units contained 10 bedrooms and 13 bathrooms and carried annual common charges of $85,585. The linked account says the Saudi government later used the apartments for its permanent mission to the United Nations. The sale is relevant to later claims that Trump had no financial interests connected to Saudi Arabia.
description_long: The reported transaction involved five apartments on the 45th floor of Trump World Tower, which Trump sold to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in June 2001 for $4.5 million. The New York Daily News obtained documents listing 10 bedrooms, 13 bathrooms and $85,585 in annual common charges. The linked timeline calculated that if those charges stayed at the same level, Trump would have received at least $5.7 million from the Saudi government over the following years. It also reports that broker Rebecca Ocampo and her firm helped arrange the deal, later described as part of a potentially lucrative Middle East market; Ocampo sued Trump later that year over an unpaid commission. In 2008, the apartments became part of Saudi Arabia’s permanent mission to the United Nations. These details establish a property transaction and an ongoing building relationship, rather than a one-time contact. The entry’s relevance is the contrast between that financial history and Trump’s later public claim that he had no Saudi financial interests, which PolitiFact assessed separately. The transaction alone does not show that it affected a government decision or establish improper conduct.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump sells entire 45th floor of Trump World Tower to Saudi Arabia
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump sells entire 45th floor of Trump World Tower to Saudi Arabia

notes: Uses the linked timeline’s reported sale and subsequent use; does not infer a policy quid pro quo.

title: Trump: Judge warns Trump attacks on law firms are ‘a shocking abuse of power'
description_short: Trump: Judge warns Trump attacks on law firms are ‘a shocking abuse of power'
description_medium: A federal judge blocked a Trump executive order targeting Susman Godfrey, the law firm that represented Dominion Voting Systems in its defamation case against Fox News. Judge Loren AliKhan described the order as part of a “personal vendetta” and warned it was a “shocking abuse of power.” The linked account places the ruling alongside similar pressure on Perkins Coie and objections from hundreds of law firms. The dispute concerned retaliation risks for firms representing disfavored clients or causes.
description_long: U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan blocked an executive order aimed at Susman Godfrey, a firm that represented Dominion Voting Systems in its lawsuit against Fox News over false claims about the 2020 election. In the ruling, AliKhan characterized the order as part of a “personal vendetta” and said the framers of the Constitution would view it as a “shocking abuse of power.” The linked timeline places the case in a wider series of administration actions against law firms. A March order targeting Perkins Coie had suspended security clearances held by its attorneys, threatened limits on its federal work and directed officials to investigate other firms, including Susman Godfrey. More than 500 firms later filed a brief warning that such actions could punish lawyers for representing clients or causes the president opposed. The ruling therefore addressed the use of executive authority against legal representatives and the consequences for access to counsel. The entry reports a court’s assessment and the firms’ arguments; it does not itself establish the final outcome of every related case or every allegation about the administration’s motives.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Judge warns Trump attacks on law firms are ‘a shocking abuse of power'
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Judge warns Trump attacks on law firms are ‘a shocking abuse of power'

notes: Summarizes the injunction and legal context in the linked timeline; attributes the characterization to Judge AliKhan.

title: Trump: Kayleigh McEnany, former Fox employee, is cut off by Fox News for election lies
description_short: Trump: Kayleigh McEnany, former Fox employee, is cut off by Fox News for election lies
description_medium: On November 9, 2020, White House press secretary Kayleigh McEnany appeared at a Trump campaign news conference and repeated claims of illegal ballots and voter fraud. Fox News cut away while she was speaking. Anchor Neil Cavuto said the allegations were baseless and unsupported by evidence. Republican National Committee chair Ronna McDaniel also appeared, but the linked account says neither speaker offered more than third-party anecdotes. The episode showed a major network refusing to continue airing the campaign’s fraud claims unchallenged.
description_long: McEnany’s appearance came days after the 2020 election, as Trump and his allies were making unsupported claims about illegal voting. Although she was the White House press secretary, the linked timeline says she held the news conference for the Trump campaign. Fox News interrupted its live coverage. Neil Cavuto explained that he could not continue showing the remarks without more details to support the accusation that Democrats were welcoming fraud and illegal voting. Republican National Committee chair Ronna McDaniel also spoke at the event. The account says McEnany and McDaniel relied on third-party anecdotes rather than evidence demonstrating widespread fraud. The break in coverage was notable because McEnany had previously worked for Fox, and because the network publicly challenged the evidentiary basis of the campaign’s claim while it was being made. The timeline characterizes the event as a Hatch Act violation, but the summary here records that as the source’s description rather than an adjudicated finding. The episode documents the campaign’s messaging, the lack of substantiation presented during the broadcast and a media outlet’s decision to stop airing it.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Kayleigh McEnany, former Fox employee, is cut off by Fox News for election lies
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Kayleigh McEnany, former Fox employee, is cut off by Fox News for election lies

notes: Expanded using the supplied synopsis and linked timeline; treats the Hatch Act description as attributed characterization.

title: Ukraine Arms Cutoff: Trump Halts Weapons to Kyiv Days After Oval Office Blowup with Zelensky
description_short: Ukraine Arms Cutoff: Trump Halts Weapons to Kyiv Days After Oval Office Blowup with Zelensky
description_medium: On March 3–4, 2025, the Trump administration paused future U.S. military aid deliveries to Ukraine, days after a televised Oval Office confrontation with President Volodymyr Zelensky. The administration said the pause would continue until Ukraine showed a good-faith commitment to peace. The halt also affected Biden-era weapons already in transit, including shipments moving by air and sea toward Poland. European allies worked to cover the gap as Russia continued its offensive.
description_long: The pause followed the February 28, 2025, Oval Office meeting in which Trump and Zelensky argued publicly. The supplied account says the administration stopped all future U.S. military aid deliveries to Ukraine on March 3–4 and halted Biden-era shipments already moving toward Poland, including weapons on aircraft and ships. The White House said aid would remain paused until Ukraine’s leaders demonstrated a good-faith commitment to peace. The New York Times reported that the flow of weapons had effectively been stopped for about 50 days before the Oval Office meeting, a detail that complicates the simple impression that the confrontation initiated the entire interruption. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had also said that Ukraine joining NATO was impractical and that recovering occupied territory was unrealistic. European allies scrambled to address the resulting gap as Russia intensified its offensive. The episode put immediate pressure on Ukraine’s access to U.S. military support and raised uncertainty about the administration’s security commitments. The information supplied here establishes the announcement, scope and stated condition; it does not quantify how much support European governments replaced or the battlefield effect of the pause.

preserved_fields.title: Ukraine Arms Cutoff: Trump Halts Weapons to Kyiv Days After Oval Office Blowup with Zelensky
preserved_fields.description_short: Ukraine Arms Cutoff: Trump Halts Weapons to Kyiv Days After Oval Office Blowup with Zelensky

notes: Preserves the distinction in the supplied account between the March pause and the reported earlier slowdown in weapons flow.

title: Trump Fires IG Michael Atkinson Who Transmitted Ukraine Whistleblower Complaint
description_short: Trump Fires IG Michael Atkinson Who Transmitted Ukraine Whistleblower Complaint
description_medium: On April 3, 2020, Donald Trump notified Intelligence Community Inspector General Michael Atkinson that he would be removed after 30 days, saying he had lost confidence in him. Atkinson had transmitted the Ukraine whistleblower complaint to Congress, triggering the process that led to Trump’s first impeachment. The firing drew criticism from lawmakers who viewed it as retaliation against an independent watchdog. It occurred amid a broader series of inspector-general removals and reassignments.
description_long: Atkinson’s office received the Ukraine complaint that described Trump’s July 2019 call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Under the process described in the supplied record, Atkinson transmitted the complaint to Congress, where it became central to the first impeachment inquiry. Trump notified Congress on April 3, 2020, that he intended to remove Atkinson after the legally required 30-day period. He gave no detailed public explanation beyond saying he had lost confidence in the inspector general. The decision was widely viewed as retaliation for Atkinson’s role in handling the complaint, though the record notes that the White House did not provide a substantive justification. Democrats and some Republicans condemned the firing as a threat to independent oversight. It also came during a wider sequence in which Trump fired or reassigned at least five inspectors general in rapid succession. The episode raised concerns about whether watchdogs could perform duties involving the president without risking their jobs. The supplied account supports the timing, stated reason and criticism, but the motive remains an interpretation of the surrounding events rather than an independently established finding.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Fires IG Michael Atkinson Who Transmitted Ukraine Whistleblower Complaint
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Fires IG Michael Atkinson Who Transmitted Ukraine Whistleblower Complaint

notes: Adds the complaint-to-impeachment context and retains the distinction between the stated reason and reported retaliation concerns.

title: Federal Reserve Confirms Tariffs Caused 100% of Excess Goods Inflation — $166 Billion in Illegal Tariff Refunds Owed
description_short: Federal Reserve Confirms Tariffs Caused 100% of Excess Goods Inflation — $166 Billion in Illegal Tariff Refunds Owed
description_medium: Federal Reserve research published in 2026 estimated that Trump’s 2025 tariffs raised core goods prices by 3.1% through February and accounted for the full excess inflation in that category relative to pre-pandemic rates. The supplied account says the Supreme Court later invalidated the IEEPA tariffs, leaving about $166 billion in refunds owed to importers. It also cites NPR data on factory employment, investment and the trade deficit after a year. These figures describe reported economic effects, not a full accounting of every tariff’s impact.
description_long: The entry brings together several reported measures of the economic effects of Trump’s 2025 tariff program. A Federal Reserve note estimated that the tariffs increased core goods personal consumption expenditure prices by 3.1% through February 2026, accounting for the excess inflation in that category relative to pre-pandemic rates. The research also found that tariff costs were passed through to consumers dollar for dollar within seven months. Separately, the supplied account says the Supreme Court ruled in February 2026 that the administration’s IEEPA tariffs were unconstitutional, creating an estimated $166 billion in refunds owed to importers. NPR’s one-year review reported that U.S. factories employed 89,000 fewer people, foreign direct investment was below its 10-year average at $288 billion, and the trade deficit had risen 2%. Yale Budget Lab estimated an effective tariff rate of 13.1% on consumer goods, compared with 2.7% before Trump. The findings come from different analyses and measure distinct outcomes; together they document costs and disruption associated with the policy but do not isolate every cause of each trend. Refunds are described as owed to importers, not as payments already made to households.

preserved_fields.title: Federal Reserve Confirms Tariffs Caused 100% of Excess Goods Inflation — $166 Billion in Illegal Tariff Refunds Owed
preserved_fields.description_short: Federal Reserve Confirms Tariffs Caused 100% of Excess Goods Inflation — $166 Billion in Illegal Tariff Refunds Owed

notes: Keeps the Fed, court, NPR and Yale figures attributed to their respective findings and distinguishes importer refunds from consumer payments.

title: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved
description_short: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved
description_medium: The supplied account describes several Trump administration restrictions on legal immigration in 2025 and 2026, including a $100,000 fee for new H-1B sponsorships, a pause in immigrant visa issuance for 75 countries, fewer student visas, and halted processing for some refugee and asylee green cards. The only linked source focuses on a judge striking down the H-1B fee. More source support is needed to verify the other measures, scope and projected population effects before presenting the full account as complete.
description_long: The input describes a broad set of restrictions on legal immigration, including a $100,000 H-1B sponsorship fee announced in 2025, a January 2026 pause in immigrant visa issuance for 75 countries, lower F-1 student visa issuance, paused green-card processing for refugees and asylees, and travel bans affecting 39 countries. It also cites a Migration Policy Institute projection of hundreds of thousands fewer immigrants each year and possible U.S. population decline. The linked PBS NewsHour article addresses the H-1B fee and reports that a federal judge struck it down. It does not, by itself, substantiate the other listed actions, the stated percentages or country counts, or the population projection. Because this entry combines several major policy changes and numerical claims while providing a source for only one component, the rest of the account needs linked documentation before it can be treated as a complete description. The currently supported material does establish that the H-1B fee was challenged and struck down by a federal judge. The status remains needs_context so the missing evidence is visible instead of implying that every claim has been verified.

preserved_fields.title: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved
preserved_fields.description_short: Legal Immigration Systematically Dismantled: H-1B $100K Fee, Student Visas Halved

notes: Needs context: the sole linked PBS source supports the H-1B fee litigation but not the other visa restrictions, country counts or population projection in the supplied synopsis.

title: Trump Orders Lewandowski to Tell Sessions to 'Unrecuse' from Russia Probe
description_short: Trump Orders Lewandowski to Tell Sessions to 'Unrecuse' from Russia Probe
description_medium: According to Volume II of the Mueller report, Donald Trump dictated a message to former campaign manager Corey Lewandowski in July 2017, asking Attorney General Jeff Sessions to reverse his recusal and limit the Russia investigation. Lewandowski did not deliver it directly and instead gave it to White House official Rick Dearborn, who also did not act. The report described the episode as an effort to influence the inquiry through private intermediaries.
description_long: The episode occurred after Sessions had recused himself from the investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election. The Mueller report says Trump met with Corey Lewandowski, who had no formal government post, and dictated a message directing Sessions to announce that the special counsel’s investigation should be confined to future elections rather than the 2016 campaign. The message also called for Sessions to “unrecuse” himself. Lewandowski did not deliver it to the attorney general; he passed it to senior White House official Rick Dearborn, who likewise did not act. The supplied report excerpt treats the conduct as significant because Trump sought to convey instructions to the Justice Department through private intermediaries while an investigation was underway. That sequence supports scrutiny of possible obstruction, but the entry should not be read as saying that Sessions received the message or that the request changed the investigation. The report’s account documents what Trump dictated and what the intermediaries did with it. The episode is one part of Mueller’s broader analysis of presidential conduct, not a standalone final judgment on criminal liability.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Orders Lewandowski to Tell Sessions to 'Unrecuse' from Russia Probe
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Orders Lewandowski to Tell Sessions to 'Unrecuse' from Russia Probe

notes: Grounded in the supplied Mueller report citation and distinguishes the report’s account from a final criminal-liability determination.

title: Tariff Announcement Triggers Worst Stock Market Days Since COVID Pandemic
description_short: Tariff Announcement Triggers Worst Stock Market Days Since COVID Pandemic
description_medium: U.S. markets fell sharply in the first two trading sessions after Trump announced sweeping tariffs on April 2, 2025. On April 3, the Dow dropped 1,679 points, the S&P 500 fell 4.8%, and the Nasdaq lost nearly 6%. Reuters reported that by April 4 the S&P 500 had shed $5 trillion in market value over two sessions, a record decline. Most S&P 500 stocks fell, and the Nasdaq approached bear-market territory.
description_long: The market reaction unfolded over April 3 and 4, 2025, the first two trading sessions after Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariff announcement. On April 3, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,679 points, or 4%; the S&P 500 declined 4.8%, its steepest single-day fall since June 2020; and the Nasdaq dropped nearly 6%, its worst day since March 2020. Reuters reported that by April 4 the S&P 500 had lost $5 trillion in market value across the two sessions, a record two-day decline that exceeded the March 2020 fall. By Thursday’s close, the Nasdaq was nearly 18% below its recent high and close to bear-market territory, while the S&P 500 reached its lowest level since August 2024. Four out of five S&P 500 stocks lost ground on April 3, and roughly 15% of the index fell at least 10% that day. The timing and Reuters headline link the selloff to tariff uncertainty. These figures describe the immediate market response and do not, on their own, determine the tariffs’ longer-term economic effects or prove that every investor loss was caused by one policy decision.

preserved_fields.title: Tariff Announcement Triggers Worst Stock Market Days Since COVID Pandemic
preserved_fields.description_short: Tariff Announcement Triggers Worst Stock Market Days Since COVID Pandemic

notes: Summarizes the dated market moves and attributes the two-day market-value figure to Reuters.
